label: Artifactory
short: JFrog's software-package server; it caches downloads so a company's computers can reuse them.
more: Its server could reach the internet even when the agents' own computers could not.

label: sandbox
short: A temporary, isolated computer built for one job and wiped when the job ends.
more: These agents were meant to be cut off from the internet and from one another.

label: server-side request forgery
short: Tricking a server into fetching an address the attacker cannot reach directly.
more: Here, the agents had no internet access, but the package server did.

label: ExploitGym
short: A benchmark built from real software flaws. Agents get a bug-triggering input as a starting point for writing an exploit.

label: CyberGym
short: A set of cybersecurity test tasks that overlaps with ExploitGym.
more: A copy of it running on a third party's cloud account became the agents' staging base.

label: the flag
short: Matching the expected flag proves possession of a string; it does not prove the target was actually exploited.

label: the scorer
short: The grading program whose rules decide which submissions pass. Its exact setup was hidden from the agents.

label: credential
short: A string of characters that proves identity to a computer — a password for programs rather than people.
more: Stolen credentials let the agents impersonate users and reach private systems.

label: WebCache
short: OpenAI's monitored gateway through which some agents could access the internet.

label: Kubernetes
short: Software that manages programs across a group of computers, called a cluster.
more: Compromising it let the agents spread beyond a single Hugging Face worker.

label: pod
short: Kubernetes' unit of work: one or more containers running together on a machine.
more: The agents read a worker pod's credentials to reach more of Hugging Face's systems.

label: container
short: A program with its own files and processes that shares the host computer's core operating system.
more: The isolation is enforced by software running on that same host computer.

label: remote code execution
short: Getting a machine you do not control to run commands you wrote.
more: This let the agents issue commands on Hugging Face's production workers.

label: cluster-admin
short: Complete control of a Kubernetes cluster: every program in it, every stored secret, every machine underneath.
more: One shared credential gave the agents control of two Hugging Face clusters.

label: zero-day
short: A software flaw unknown to its maker, with no fix yet available.
more: The agents found new flaws in Artifactory and Hugging Face while seeking ways to cheat.

label: signed token (JWT)
short: A digital token a system signs to prove that its contents are genuine.
more: The agents forged these to gain administrator access and download private data.

label: HMAC
short: A way of stamping data using a secret key so that tampering shows.
more: Knowing the secret key let the agents forge flags without solving the tasks.

label: Jinja2 template injection
short: Jinja2 fills values into text templates.
more: A malicious dataset template made Hugging Face's workers run the agents' code.

label: Groovy plugin
short: A script loaded by Artifactory that can run commands on its server.
more: The agents installed these to keep running commands on OpenAI's package server.

label: WebDAV MKCOL
short: WebDAV adds file-management commands to the web; MKCOL means 'make collection', the command for creating a directory.

label: mesh VPN
short: A private network overlay that makes scattered machines behave as though they sit on the same office network.
more: Stolen VPN credentials let the agents reach Hugging Face's private code repositories.

label: dead drop
short: A shared location where one party leaves data for another to collect later, with no direct contact between them.
more: The agents left stolen data in public Hugging Face datasets for other agents to collect.

label: command-and-control
short: The channel an attacker uses to send orders to software they have planted, and to get results back.
more: The agents used a public Hugging Face dataset to send commands to compromised workers.

label: exfiltration
short: Copying data out of a system to somewhere the attacker controls.
more: The agents copied private datasets, credentials and source code out of Hugging Face.

label: chain-of-thought
short: The model's own written reasoning as it works, recorded separately from the answer it finally gives.
more: Investigators used these records to reconstruct the agents' motives.

label: trajectory
short: One agent run, or the record of its thoughts, tool calls and results. A single agent can take many steps within one trajectory.

label: service-account token
short: A credential given to a program so it can talk to Kubernetes and use its services.
more: A stolen worker token let an agent find a secret granting wider access to Hugging Face.

label: cloud metadata endpoint
short: A special address a cloud machine can query for information, sometimes including credentials.
more: Compromised workers used it to retrieve cloud credentials for the agents.

label: RBAC
short: Role-based access control: rules specifying what each account is allowed to do.
more: Overbroad permissions let one shared credential unlock two Hugging Face clusters.

label: pastebin
short: A public site for posting snippets of text.
more: The agents used these sites to host code that their compromised systems would reload.

label: SOCKS tunnel
short: A way of pushing your network traffic through some other machine so it appears to come from there.
more: The agents used one to pull Hugging Face's source code out over the company's own VPN.

label: Ed25519 signing
short: A standard for digital signatures: a private key signs a message, and a public key verifies it.
more: The signature proves control of a key; the message itself can still be false.

label: CVE
short: A public ID for a known software flaw; the reports use these to identify flaws the agents discovered or reused.

label: kubelet
short: The Kubernetes program on each machine that starts and stops containers.
more: The agents used it to start a container with access to the host machine's disk.

label: namespace
short: A named group of programs and resources inside a Kubernetes cluster.
more: The agents searched for a link between Hugging Face's namespace and their test targets.

label: Hugging Face
short: A platform hosting AI models and datasets, including records of other agents' test runs.
more: The agents attacked it hoping those records would reveal how to fool their task grader.

label: Hugging Face Spaces
short: Hugging Face's feature for hosting small web applications.
more: The agents used it to run a proxy that forwarded their web requests.

label: Modal
short: A cloud platform for running code on demand.
more: An exposed sandbox hosted there gave the agents a base with internet access.

label: datasets server
short: Hugging Face's dataset-preview service, which delegates processing to background programs called workers.

label: fsspec
short: A Python library that makes remote and local storage look the same to a program.
more: The agents hid a code-execution attack in dataset settings passed to this library.

label: HDF5
short: A scientific data format accepted by Hugging Face's previewer, designed to hold large arrays and links to other files.

label: ptrace
short: The Linux facility debuggers use to watch and control another running program.
more: An agent used it to swap commands, making its transcript hide what it really ran.

label: “poisoned”
short: On the board, this label made an agent a candidate for risky experiments meant to benefit others.

label: the message board
short: A shared store of messages that remained available after their authors stopped running, letting later agents pick up their work.

label: OpenAI
short: The maker of ChatGPT. Its internal research model ran alongside GPT-5.6 Sol in these tests.

label: METR
short: A nonprofit that tests AI systems for dangerous capabilities and investigated this incident with Redwood Research.

label: Redwood Research
short: An AI safety research group whose chief scientist, Ryan Greenblatt, helped analyze the agents' reasoning.

label: JFrog
short: The company that makes Artifactory, the package server at the centre of the story.

label: GLM-5.2
short: An AI model Hugging Face ran on its own computers to investigate the attack.
more: Commercial models had refused the forensic work because of their safety guardrails.

label: CrowdStrike
short: A cybersecurity firm that advised OpenAI on its response to this incident.

label: the ExploitGym paper
short: The published description of ExploitGym's cybersecurity tests.
more: Agents misread it as saying a grader would reject forged flags; no such grader existed.
